searchText: It looks like we can parse the prefix witness by the existing code with minimal changes, if we just traverse it backwards. I implemented the code here: https://github.com/ledgerwatch/turbo-geth/compare/prefix-witness-parse-backwards It will lose streamability of course. But I don't think it is a big problem because we want to split it to chunks and propagate chunks around. That way it doesn't matter if we can stream a single chunk or not. This code is PoC, it creates prefix witnesses for the mainnet, and runs blocks using them. It is the same way we tested all our algorithms. excerpts.author: mandrigin
excerpts.content:
It looks like we can parse the prefix witness by the existing code with minimal changes, if we just traverse it backwards. I implemented the code here:  https://github.com/ledgerwatch/turbo-geth/compare/prefix-witness-parse-backwards

It will lose streamability of course.
But I don't think it is a big problem because we want to split it to chunks and propagate chunks around.
That way it doesn't matter if we can stream a single chunk or not.

excerpts.author: mandrigin
excerpts.content:
This code is PoC, it creates prefix witnesses for the mainnet, and runs blocks using them. It is the same way we tested all our algorithms.
I tested it successfully on first 900.000 first blocks, it works (the test is still running in background).

A candidate Merkle root is computed using the data provided and its Merkle proof, which is then matched against an expected root. But I see in the high-level algorithm that len(witness) is checked with 1, and also correspondingly defined in the section on “Success criteria: a single trie". If my understanding is correct, even when there is one trie to be constructed, the proofs can end up with multiple nodes in the top. In fact, there should be 15 nodes.
